rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /\b(wound|dressing|npwt|negative[- ]pressure|pressure area care)\b/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on.
rules.suppliers: Every supplier NHS Supply Chain names on the frameworks above, resolved to one name per company through the Hub's alias registry, and ordered by how many of this speciality's frameworks they appear on. That count is the only claim made. It is not a ranking of size or share. Where NHS Supply Chain spelled a company two ways across its own pages, both spellings are shown against the one entry.
rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(wound|woundcare|dressing|dressings|npwt|negative[- ]pressure wound|tissue viability|pressure ulcer|pressure sore|pressure relieving|pressure area care|debridement|larval therapy|compression (?:bandag|hosiery|garment|therapy|stocking)|lymphoedema|bandag(?:e|ing)|skin integrity|wound closure|suture|leg ulcer|diabetic foot|venous ulcer|honey dressing|silver dressing|foam dressing|hydrocolloid|alginate)\b/i and does not match /\b(seed viability|eye tissue|corneal|toilet tissue|paper hygiene|facial tissue|chest compression|test rig|laminar flow|pressure infus|blood pressure|pressure washer|tissue culture|breast tissue|soft tissue (?:sarcoma|imaging))\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. A CPV code beginning 3314111 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IXA for the stated effective month, summarised. Prices are the reimbursement price at publication, converted from the pence NHSBSA publishes, and are not necessarily today's.

localIntel.title: Wound Care Management Joint Formulary 2025
localIntel.fact: The change log records Zetuvit and Eclypse removed and replaced with ConvaMax. HydroClean Advance and Atrauman remain listed.
localIntel.quote: Removal of Zetuvits and Eclypse dressings to be replaced with Convamax
localIntel.use: A named formulary switch between competitors.

localIntel.title: Wound Care Formulary, September 2025
localIntel.fact: Lists RespoSorb Silicone Border in seven sizes with NHS Supply Chain codes (e.g. EJA254), Atrauman and Cosmopor. Under compression it names Kliniderm Superabsorbent and RespoSorb Silicone Border.
localIntel.quote: This August 2025 edition replaces the previous February
localIntel.use: Which brands are on formulary, with order codes.

localIntel.org: Oxford Health NHS FT and Oxford University Hospitals
localIntel.title: Wound Formulary Comparison Guidance V2, November 2025
localIntel.fact: Maps community products to their acute equivalents, e.g. community Kliniderm Foam Silicone Border against acute RespoSorb Silicone Border. Zetuvit Plus, Atrauman and Cosmopor E also appear.
localIntel.use: Shows where a patient's dressing changes between hospital and community in one ICB.

localIntel.title: Wound Care Formulary by setting (webinar pack, July 2025)
localIntel.fact: Split by setting (GP, community nursing, care homes, tissue viability specialists). Zetuvit E is the basic absorbent in all four; RespoSorb Silicone and Zetuvit Plus appear in the tissue viability specialist column. HydroClean Advance, Atrauman and Cosmopor E are listed.

localIntel.title: Community Dressing Formulary 2025 V3
localIntel.fact: Lists RespoSorb Silicone (and Border), Zetuvit, Zetuvit Plus Silicone, Atrauman Ag, Cosmopor E and HydroClean.
localIntel.quote: Approved by Tissue Viability October 2025 – Review 2027

localIntel.title: Wound Management Formulary V6.1
localIntel.fact: Lists HydroClean Advance debridement dressing and Atrauman (HARTMANN) with PIP codes. Kliniderm is named throughout.
localIntel.use: Review due within weeks: the moment to be in front of the formulary group.

localIntel.title: Joint Wound Care Formulary
localIntel.fact: Atrauman is the only HARTMANN line. The superabsorbent is KerraMax Care.

localIntel.title: Wound Management Guidelines and Formulary v2.7
localIntel.fact: Names Kliniderm Super Absorbent as first-line choice. No HARTMANN product named.

localIntel.org: NHS Shared Business Services with NHS Supply Chain
localIntel.title: SBS10518 Distribution of Advanced Wound Care
localIntel.fact: A joint NHS SBS and NHS Supply Chain procurement renewing part of the Advanced Wound Care and Lymphoedema agreement (SBS10142). £91,000,000 ex VAT. Tender period ended 24/04/2026. Award not yet verified.
localIntel.quote: This is a renewal of part of an existing NHS SBS agreement
localIntel.use: Decides how advanced wound care products reach community settings from 2027.

localIntel.title: SBS10142 Advanced Wound Care and Lymphoedema: extension
localIntel.ends: 01/08/2026 per this notice; NHS SBS's own page says 01/08/2027
localIntel.fact: A 12-month extension on existing terms to 01/08/2026, while NHS SBS collaborates with other framework hosts on the next generation of the agreement. No Find a Tender notice for a further year to 2027 was found.
localIntel.quote: a 12 month extension on existing terms, bringing the end date to 1 August 2026
localIntel.use: Why the SBS renewal is late, and why the end date needs checking before quoting.

localIntel.title: Advanced Wound Care award
localIntel.fact: Two lots: 30 suppliers on Lot 1 and 56 on Lot 2, which is 59 distinct names. Absorbest, Advanced Medical Solutions and GBUK appear only in Lot 1. Paul Hartmann Ltd is awarded. The launch brief states 56 suppliers, which does not reconcile with the 59 distinct names on this award notice.
localIntel.use: Reconciles the supplier count: 59 distinct companies across both lots.

localIntel.title: Surgical Dressings
localIntel.fact: £56.1m ex VAT across 11 lots, e.g. Securement & Dressings £14,584,364 and single-use NPWT systems £6,977,241. Who won is not verified.
localIntel.use: Northern Ireland market size by lot.

localIntel.title: Wound Management framework
localIntel.fact: £28,339,827 estimated, with lots including alginates, hydrogels, hydrocolloids and absorbent fibre. No award notice found on Find a Tender; winners not verified.

localIntel.title: Drug Tariff Part IX categorisation, Wave 2 (Wound and skin care) v2.0
localIntel.fact: Assigns every wound product to a cluster for the Wave 2 review, e.g. 'Superabsorbent dressing, with silicone wound contact layer, adhesive', 'Hydro-responsive dressing' and 'Low adherent silicone permeable wound contact layer'.
localIntel.quote: Newly added clusters are highlighted yellow
localIntel.use: Tells a supplier which cluster each product will be benchmarked in when Wave 2 renewals open.

localIntel.title: Spend over £25,000, 2026 (January to August)
localIntel.fact: Across 3,888 rows, 154 payments to NHS Supply Chain total about £72.5m (all categories). There is no Paul Hartmann payment at £25k or more, and one TJ Smith & Nephew line (£28,572.89, February 2026).
localIntel.use: Acute dressing spend flows through NHS Supply Chain, so trust spend files understate each manufacturer's acute share.
